oneTimers: Costs tied to the July 19 Incident and related matters were $35.7M in the quarter, vs $5.1M a year ago.
Charges tied to the May 2025 strategic plan — cutting about 500 roles, 5% of the workforce — were $38.4M, mostly severance ($20.1M) and stock pay ($17.9M).
Stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes were $284.2M — the main reason non-GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike ($237.4M) contrasts with the GAAP attributable net loss ($77.7M).
otherDetail: Interest income of $50.9M, less $6.8M of interest expense and $2.7M of other costs, net — a net $41.3M gain outside operations.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: The Falcon security platform, sold by subscription — 94% of all revenue.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Security experts for hire — incident response and setup help.

takeaways.text: Net new ARR — new subscription value signed in the quarter — hit a record $221.1M, taking ending ARR to $4.66B, up 20% year over year. Over 1,000 customers are now on the Flex subscription model.
takeaways.title: Record new business

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $113.0M as $284.2M of stock-based pay weighed, plus $35.7M of July 19 Incident costs and $38.4M of strategic-plan charges; non-GAAP operating income was a record $255.0M.
takeaways.title: In the red on paper

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was a Q2-record $283.6M on $332.8M of operating cash flow, and cash grew to a record $4.97B — CrowdStrike's cash generation is far stronger than its GAAP result suggests.
takeaways.title: Cash flow tells another story

verdict: CrowdStrike grew revenue 21% to $1.17B and signed a record $221M of new subscription business, but stock pay, outage costs and a restructuring charge kept the quarter in the red — a $78M net loss — even as non-GAAP profit hit a record $237M.
